source_defaults.notes: Candidate's own answers in original Patch profiles published and last modified before the June23 primary. Reporter introductions, subscription prompts, endorsement lists and allegations about opponents are not adopted as independently verified findings.

sources.speaker: Eliot L. Engel
sources.identity_notes: The publisher identifies Eliot Engel as the incumbent seeking reelection in NY16; the canonical primary record includes his middle initial. Explicit reviewed same-office display-name association.

statements.claim: Supports Medicare for All as healthcare as a human right, without patients having to worry about premiums, deductibles and copays.
Supports a Green New Deal linking decarbonization, union jobs, racial equity, education and a global transition.
Names inequality as the most pressing issue and connects racial injustice, health, policing, environment and violence to a Reconstruction Agenda.

statements.quote: empowering organized communities on the outside
statements.claim: Proposes combining an inside congressional platform with organized communities and social movements outside government.
Supports a Homes Guarantee, federal tenant protections and equitable zoning, plus the proposed $180-billion Green New Deal for public housing.

statements.quote: shift funding and resources from police departments
statements.claim: Explicitly proposes shifting funding from police, jails and prisons to new public-health agencies. No opponent's contrary position is inferred from silence.

statements.quote: fighting for women's reproductive rights, Medicare for All
statements.claim: Explicitly says he fights for Medicare for All; elsewhere describes founding caucus membership, building on the ACA and expanding Medicare. The source does not support an ACA-only label.

statements.quote: building an economy that works under the Green New Deal
statements.claim: Explicitly supports a Green New Deal and describes himself as an original sponsor.

statements.quote: The catastrophic and corrupt Trump presidency.
statements.claim: Names the Trump presidency as the most pressing issue and emphasizes defending reproductive, environmental, healthcare and civil rights.

statements.quote: my experience and position in Democratic leadership
statements.claim: Presents experience and leadership relationships as the way to bring federal resources to the district. His claimed effectiveness is not independently measured here.
Supports implementing a Green New Deal and frames project-financing and renewable-energy experience as his qualification.
Proposes a carbon-neutral grid by2040, transit modernization, electric-vehicle charging, efficient buildings, Paris reentry and redirecting fossil-fuel subsidies.
Names the climate crisis as the most pressing issue and describes concrete infrastructure measures.

statements.quote: 32 years of experience implementing renewable energy projects
statements.claim: Campaigns on technical implementation experience. His claim of being uniquely qualified is not independently endorsed.

statements.quote: improving on the Affordable Care Act
statements.claim: Proposes access for all Americans by improving the ACA. This does not establish categorical opposition to every single-payer proposal.
Names jobs lost during the pandemic as the pressing concern and proposes an infrastructure bill to create jobs and support small businesses.
Promises monthly town halls and returning to the district each weekend when legislative sessions permit.

statements.quote: raising the minimum federal wage to $15
statements.claim: Supports a $15 federal minimum wage as an income-inequality measure.

comparisons.analysis: Both explicitly support Medicare for All in their own pre-primary answers. Engel also describes ACA and Medicare expansion; that does not erase his stated Medicare-for-All support or prove identical implementation plans.
Both explicitly support a Green New Deal. The challenger/incumbent conflict is not evidence of opposing positions on that named proposal.
Both support a Green New Deal. Bowman connects it to racial equity, union jobs and education; Fink emphasizes implementation and project-financing experience.
Bowman specifies Medicare for All; Ravelo proposes universal access by improving the ACA. These are different stated reform approaches, without inventing an explicit Ravelo rejection of single payer.

Bowman organizes his answer around racial and economic inequality and a Reconstruction Agenda; Engel names opposing Trump and defending rights as the immediate priority. Their healthcare and climate commitments nevertheless overlap.
Bowman names inequality; Fink names climate. Both also support climate investment, so different lead messages are not opposing policy goals.

Bowman emphasizes structural racial and economic inequality; Ravelo emphasizes pandemic job losses and infrastructure employment. Their chosen answers to the same question differ, without measuring whole-campaign message frequency.
Bowman proposes linking congressional power to organized communities and outside movements; Engel emphasizes seniority and relationships within Democratic leadership to deliver resources.
Bowman emphasizes inside-outside movement organization; Fink emphasizes project-finance and implementation expertise. Neither claim independently establishes effectiveness.
Bowman emphasizes community movement power and a congressional public platform; Ravelo gives a regular district-presence and town-hall commitment. These methods can coexist.
